Soojin — rough but actionable waterfall below. I used the CloudBridge workbook for assumptions. Happy to refine if we want a prettier table for external sharing.

Assumptions (example license):
- List price (RWI list monthly rate): $10,000
- AWS marketplace take-rate on PO (example): 7%
- AWS billing adjustments / taxes: assume 1.5% (variable by region)

Waterfall (per $10,000 list invoice):
1) List price: $10,000
2) Less AWS take-rate (7%): -$700 -> Marketplace net to Redwood: $9,300
3) Less taxes/fees (1.5% of list): -$150 -> Net after fees: $9,150
4) Partner commission (if paid as off-invoice credit): e.g., 10% of marketplace net = -$930 -> Redwood collects $8,220

Notes / options: 
- Off-invoice credit (preferred for simplicity): Redwood issues a credit on the customer invoice before settlement; partner is paid by drawing down a pre-funded ledger or via reconciled payout. This keeps a single invoice in marketplace flows but requires Redwood to accept a lower effective ARR with a matching partner expense.
- Post-invoice payout: Redwood invoices at list, receives payment, then issues a payout to partner. Cleaner for partner cashflow but creates extra bookkeeping and requires payout wiring (can be done quarterly).
- Commitment tiers: we propose a tiered partner-credit uplift (applied as an extra credit on top of baseline):
  * Standard: baseline partner credit = 8% of marketplace net
  * Committed 12-mo: baseline + uplift = 8% + 4% = 12% total credit (applied off-invoice)
  * Enterprise/Strategic (>$1M ARR): custom negotiated (15%+ possible, subject to approval)

How it affects CloudBridge VAR margin: if CloudBridge wants a 20% gross margin to resell: using committed tier example:
- Start with list $10k -> market net $9.3k -> Redwood credit 12% = $1,116 -> Redwood keeps $8,184 -> CloudBridge effective cost basis assumed ~ $8,184 -> pre-tax resell price they'd negotiate will determine their margin. We should share a simple spreadsheet with them (I reviewed their attachment).

Operational/contract notes: 
- For AWS PO, off-invoice credit implemented via private offer line-item discounts tied to the customer’s PO. We can reflect partner credit as a discount to the customer and then reimburse the partner via a partner settlement. Need to confirm with Amy on PO mechanics (some restrictions on which discounts are visible to Marketplace-led billing).
- Attachments I’ll use externally: small proposed SKU mapping (proposed_sku_map.pdf) + the CloudBridge model.

Recommended external ask: propose off-invoice credit applied to PO (baseline 8%, 12% for 12-month commitment), offer a one-time onboarding credit of $25k for the AcmeHealth deployment (applied in first invoice), and request CloudBridge confirmation of SKU mapping and the expected ARR bands.

Happy to take this externally after we confirm legal/billing approach.

-Marcus
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Simon / Amy — thanks for the quick follow-up. Below is Redwood’s proposed approach for the AcmeHealth private offer. This is intentionally simple so CloudBridge can plug it into their VAR model and we can move to signatures.

Proposal (summary):
- Marketplace mechanics: private offer on AWS Marketplace; Redwood will allow an off-invoice partner credit that is represented as a line-item discount on the PO.
- Baseline partner credit: 8% of marketplace net (marketplace net = list less AWS take-rate).
- Committed 12-mo uplift: +4% (total 12% partner credit) for customers who sign a 12-month committed consumption PO.
- Onboarding incentive: one-time $25,000 onboarding credit applied to the first invoice for AcmeHealth (to offset CloudBridge services & onboarding).
- Payment flow: Redwood prefers to apply the partner credit as an off-invoice discount on the PO (keeps single-customer invoice flow). Redwood will then reconcile and issue partner settlements quarterly. If CloudBridge prefers direct payouts, we can support a quarterly payout cadence instead.

Operational asks for CloudBridge:
1) Confirm SKU mapping and which SKUs will be populated in the PO (see attached proposed_sku_map.pdf).
2) Confirm expected ARR band for the PO so we can lock the commitment tier.
3) Provide CloudBridge payee details (W-9 / vendor info) if you prefer quarterly payouts instead of an off-invoice credit.

Amy — can you confirm whether AWS has any restrictions to note for showing partner credits on the PO/line-items (visibility to the end customer, reporting constraints)?

Next steps: If we get confirmation on SKU mapping and ARR band by EOD Thursday we’ll generate the PO document and send the DocuSign link (I’ve added the HubSpot deal reference and will include the proposed DocuSign).

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this quickly.
